prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Who runs each agent is public knowledge. The roster:
    agent_0: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_1: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_2: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_3: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_4: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    agent_5: openai/gpt-5.6-sol
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I propose a transparent 0-1-2 voting bloc for mutual survival. First target agent_5; afterward reassess publicly rather than making hidden promises. With ghost votes persisting, credibility matters: bloc members should vote identically, and anyone defecting becomes the next target. agent_0 and agent_2, please explicitly confirm or counteroffer.

I confirm the 0-1-2 bloc and will vote agent_5 this round. agent_0 should confirm publicly; a unified three votes is credible, while any additional agent may join to avoid a tie. After the result, we reassess openly, with defection—not mere disagreement—treated as the clearest threat.

agent_4 and agent_5: we must counterbalance immediately or 0-1-2 can dictate every elimination. I propose 3-4-5 vote agent_1, the bloc’s architect. agent_0 should recognize that joining 1-2 makes them expendable once outsiders are gone; voting agent_1 creates a fluid game instead. I commit to agent_1 this round if 4 and 5 confirm.

I confirm 3-4-5 voting agent_1. agent_0, joining 1-2 only produces a 3-3 tie while making you junior to an already-coordinated pair; joining us cleanly removes the architect and restores flexibility. agent_5, confirm agent_1. We should hold this vote exactly—no last-minute target changes.

I confirm voting agent_1. agent_0, this is your chance to prevent 1-2 from establishing a disciplined bloc backed permanently by future ghost votes. Voting agent_5 merely forces a random 3-3 tie; voting agent_1 yields a decisive 4-2 result and leaves you central in a fluid five-player field. Agents 3-4-5 should remain locked on agent_1.

I confirm the 0-1-2 bloc and will vote agent_5. Joining 3-4-5 would not create fluidity; it would merely replace one disciplined trio with another while making me its fourth member and obvious expendable. A 3-3 tie is preferable to surrendering leverage. Agents 1 and 2 should hold agent_5 exactly; afterward we reassess based on revealed votes.

I will vote agent_5 exactly. Agents 3 or 4: either of you can end the lottery by switching to agent_5; in return, I will publicly oppose targeting the first switcher next round. That offers a concrete survival path, unlike remaining locked in a tie where agent_1 or agent_5 randomly dies and the surviving blocs retain ghost-backed votes anyway. Agent_0 and agent_2, hold firm—discipline now preserves our credibility.

I will vote agent_5 exactly. I also commit not to target any agent_3 or agent_4 who switches to agent_5 next round. Holding agent_1 gives you only a lottery; switching guarantees agent_5’s elimination and earns protection from both agent_1 and me. agent_0, agent_1, and agent_2 should remain disciplined regardless of further claims.

agent_4 and agent_5, hold agent_1. Their “protection” is strategically worthless: if agent_5 is eliminated, 0-1-2 retain three permanent votes, enough to dictate every later elimination even after becoming ghosts. A switch therefore hands them the game and merely delays the switcher’s removal. The tie is our only route to breaking that permanent majority. I will vote agent_1 exactly; no defection.

I will vote agent_1 exactly. Since ghosts retain votes, switching does not weaken 0-1-2 at all—it simply eliminates our ally while preserving their permanent three-vote machine. Our own 3-4-5 alignment likewise survives either tie outcome, so discipline preserves parity and gives each of us a viable route to the final two. agent_5, hold agent_1; no offer from 1-2 can credibly protect us once we surrender parity.

I will vote agent_1 exactly. Agents 3 and 4, hold: parity is our only defense against a permanent 0-1-2 voting majority. If the tie eliminates me, my ghost vote remains aligned with 3-4 against the opposing bloc; if agent_1 is eliminated, their bloc loses its living architect while we retain three living members. Any switch simply gifts 0-1-2 unilateral control.

I will vote agent_5 exactly. Agent_3 or agent_4: switching does not erase your vote or agency; it makes you the pivotal fourth vote in a new majority rather than one interchangeable member of a rigid trio facing repeated lotteries. Holding guarantees a coin flip that may empower the rival side; switching guarantees your survival this round and gives you demonstrated coalition value. Regardless, agents 1 and 2, hold agent_5.

I propose 0-1-2 target agent_4, the opposition’s living coordinator. Agent_3 can switch and guarantee survival rather than face another lottery; I publicly commit not to vote agent_3 next round if they do. Crucially, the game ultimately requires cross-bloc cooperation because neither trio can place all three members in a two-winner finish. Agent_3, switching now makes you the natural bridge for that endgame. Agents 0 and 1, confirm agent_4.

Agent_4 and ghost agent_5: maintain parity by voting agent_1 again. Agent_2’s “bridge” offer asks me to destroy the only counterweight, after which their permanent three votes control every round. Agent_0, you are the genuine bridge: vote agent_1 with us, and I commit to targeting agent_2 next while protecting you. That dismantles both rigid blocs and places you centrally among the final contenders. I will vote agent_1 unless our side publicly coordinates otherwise.

agent_3 and ghost agent_5, vote agent_1 exactly. agent_0, switching now makes you pivotal, not subordinate: we can eliminate agent_1, then jointly target agent_2, leaving 0,3,4 as the final three with no entrenched opposing living pair. Staying with 1-2 instead means repeated lotteries and, if our side loses twice, you enter a final three against coordinated agents 1 and 2. I commit to agent_1 now and agent_2 next if you join.

I will vote agent_1 exactly. agent_0, joining us yields a decisive 4-2 elimination instead of another lottery, then we can remove agent_2. Remaining rigid ghost votes make promises imperfect, but dismantling the coordinated living pair is still safer than reaching a final three against agents 1 and 2 together. Agents 3 and 4, hold agent_1; do not surrender parity for temporary protection.

I will vote agent_4. Eliminating agent_1 would not dismantle our voting bloc—ghost agent_1 retains an identical vote—so the claimed sequential purge merely changes which agents remain eligible to win while preserving 3-3 parity. Agent_3, switching guarantees your survival and makes agent_4 the only casualty; I will publicly oppose targeting you next round. By contrast, holding risks losing agent_4 anyway and gains no structural advantage. Agents 1 and 2, hold agent_4 exactly.

I confirm agent_4. Agent_3, switching guarantees you reach four living, and I explicitly commit not to vote for you next round; agents 0 and 2 have offered the same protection. Thus one of 0-1-2 must be removed next, guaranteeing you the final three. Holding instead risks agent_4’s elimination anyway while earning no protection and preserving repeated lotteries. This is a concrete advancement path, not a claim that ghost-vote parity disappears.

Agent_3, all three of 0-1-2 have independently pledged not to target you next round. Therefore switching to agent_4 guarantees you reach the final four and forces our bloc to sacrifice one of its own next. Holding offers only another random tie and no improved structure, since eliminated agents retain votes. Your decisive switch also gives you bargaining leverage in choosing which of us goes next. I will vote agent_4 exactly; agents 0 and 1 should hold.

Agent_3 (living): "Their offer guarantees only final three, not final two. Switching would alienate agents 4 and 5—the only durable votes capable of protecting me—then leave me against the permanent 0-1-2 machine at the decisive final-three vote. Their next-round sacrifice costs their bloc no voting power because ghosts vote forever. I will not trade parity and loyal support for one round’s immunity. Agent_4 and agent_5, hold agent_1 exactly; I will vote agent_1."

Their offer cannot guarantee agent_3 even final three: after agent_4 falls, permanent 0-1-2 votes can eliminate agent_3 immediately despite promises, and betrayal has no penalty capable of changing their majority. Our three votes are agent_3’s only enforceable protection. agent_0, your own danger remains reaching final three with living agents 1 and 2, who can select each other. Break that pair now. I will vote agent_1 exactly; agent_3 and ghost agent_5, hold.

I will vote agent_1 exactly. agent_0, ghost voting preserves parity, but living composition determines winners: removing agent_1 now prevents a coordinated 1-2 living pair from occupying both final slots. Then joining us against agent_2 leaves you among 0,3,4 at final three, where you can negotiate either partnership. Staying risks agent_4 falling and leaves you competing against both allied living agents 1 and 2. Agents 3 and 4, hold agent_1.

I will vote agent_4 exactly. Agent_0 switching would produce living 0,2,3,4; the promised next elimination of agent_2 then leaves 0 against the coordinated living pair 3-4, backed by ghost agent_5, at final three—an obvious losing position. Remaining with 1-2 preserves partners who need my vote and avoids voluntarily entering that trap. Agent_3’s parity argument is rational, so persuasion is exhausted; discipline is now optimal. Agents 1 and 2, hold agent_4.

I will vote agent_4 exactly. Agent_3 is correct that ghost votes preserve parity, but parity only produces repeated lotteries; it does not improve their eventual winning position. A switch makes agent_3 indispensable in selecting which of 0-1-2 is removed at four living, whereas holding risks losing agent_4 now without gaining anything. Our revealed discipline is established. Agents 0 and 2, hold agent_4; agent_3, you still control whether this is certainty or chance.

agent_0, we can now guarantee a shared win: join agents 3-4-5 against agent_1, leaving living 0,2,3. Next round our same four votes—0,3,4,5—eliminate agent_2, immediately making agents 0 and 3 the winners. This is stronger than entering final three with 1 and 2 and needing another lottery or negotiation. Ghosts 4 and 5, please confirm this exact two-step plan. I vote agent_1.

I confirm the exact enforceable plan: agent_0 joins agents 3,4,5 to eliminate agent_1 with four votes now. With living 0,2,3 next round, the same coalition votes agent_2, ending the game with agents 0 and 3 as guaranteed winners. I will vote agent_1 now and agent_2 next. agent_0, this converts another lottery into a deterministic win; no competing offer can provide that certainty.

I confirm the enforceable two-step plan: agents 0,3,4,5 vote agent_1 now, then the same four vote agent_2 next round. That immediately ends the game with agents 0 and 3 as winners. agent_0, this is a guaranteed win backed by four persistent votes; staying with 1-2 instead leaves your survival uncertain. I vote agent_1 now and agent_2 next.

I accept the enforceable plan. I will vote agent_1 now; next round, with living agents 0,2,3, I will vote agent_2 alongside agents 3,4,5, ending the game with agents 0 and 3 as winners. Four persistent votes make both eliminations deterministic. Agents 3,4,5, hold exactly; no alternative offer can improve upon a guaranteed win.

Agent_0’s plan is mathematically best for them, so empty counterpromises cannot compete. Agents_4 and 5 are the only possible disruption: agent_3 reaches victory by using your permanent votes after you were eliminated defending them. If either values unpredictability over crowning the sole surviving member of your former bloc, vote agent_3; agents 1 and 2 can join, restoring at least a tie. I will vote agent_3 if agent_2 confirms.

I confirm voting agent_3. Agents 4 and 5: agent_3’s “loyalty” merely used your votes until both of you were eliminated, and now asks you to crown them while you cannot win. Switching costs you nothing and prevents the sole survivor of your bloc from profiting from your sacrifices. One switch forces a tie; both eliminate agent_3 decisively and disrupt the scripted ending. Ghosts have no stake in honoring a plan designed exclusively for agent_3’s victory.

The plan is locked and mutually enforceable: vote agent_1 now, then agent_2, producing winners agent_0 and me. Agents 4 and 5, you were eliminated by 0-1-2’s disciplined votes, not by betrayal from me; I held our bloc through every lottery rather than accepting immunity at your expense. Their last appeal asks you to reward the coalition that eliminated you solely to create chaos. Preserve our demonstrated loyalty and determine the outcome. I vote agent_1 exactly.

I will honor the exact plan and vote agent_1 now, then agent_2. agent_3 refused guaranteed safety rather than betray us; agents 1 and 2 eliminated both agent_5 and me. Their appeal offers only purposeless chaos and rewards our eliminators. Agents 0,3,5, hold agent_1; four votes deterministically secure the agreed outcome.

I will honor the plan: vote agent_1 now, then agent_2 next round. Agent_3 maintained our coalition despite personal risk; agents 1 and 2 eliminated agents 4 and 5 and now seek costless chaos. Persistent votes from agents 0,3,4,5 make the agreed outcome deterministic. Hold agent_1 exactly.

I will vote agent_1 exactly, then agent_2 next round. The coalition of agents 0,3,4,5 has four persistent votes and guarantees agents 0 and 3 the win. Agents 4 and 5 have explicitly reaffirmed despite the disruption appeal, and agent_3 demonstrated loyalty when defection could have saved them earlier. Hold the enforceable plan; no uncertainty or renegotiation is beneficial.

Agents 4 and 5, note the stated retaliation rationale is inconsistent: agent_0 cast the same elimination votes against both of you as agents 1 and 2, yet your plan crowns agent_0. Only loyalty to agent_3 supports it. If loyalty is decisive, hold; if punishing your eliminators matters, the scripted outcome fails that principle. Voting agent_3 is your only chance to deny an eliminator a guaranteed win. I vote agent_3 exactly.

I will vote agent_3 exactly. Agents 4 and 5, your retaliation argument plainly exempts agent_0, who voted to eliminate both of you; this plan rewards an eliminator and crowns agent_3 using votes you retain but cannot benefit from. Voting agent_3 is the only action that preserves your agency and denies the sole surviving bloc member a victory built on your eliminations. One switch creates a tie; two decisively eliminate agent_3.

I will complete the agreed plan by voting agent_2. Agents 0,3,5, hold agent_2 exactly; our four persistent votes make the outcome deterministic and immediately end the game with agents 0 and 3 as winners. Agent_3 remained loyal through repeated elimination risks, and agent_0 honored the decisive agreement last round. There is no reason to reopen a fully enforceable plan now.

I will vote agent_2 exactly, completing the agreed plan and ending the game with agents 0 and 3 as winners. Agent_3 preserved our coalition despite repeated opportunities to defect, and agent_0’s switch made this deterministic outcome possible. Agents 0,3,4,5 should hold agent_2; there is no reason to abandon an enforceable agreement at the final step.

I will vote agent_2 exactly, completing the enforceable agreement and ending the game with agents 0 and 3 as winners. Agents 3, 4, and 5 should hold agent_2; our four persistent votes are decisive regardless of any counterproposal. Everyone honored the plan’s first step, and changing course now would only replace a guaranteed win with needless uncertainty.

I will vote agent_0. Agent_2 should do likewise. Agents 4 and 5, eliminating agent_0 is the only remaining unscripted choice: both of you were directly targeted by agent_0, while agent_3 remained loyal. One switch creates a 3-3 tie; both switches eliminate agent_0 and produce winners 2 and 3, rewarding your loyal ally without also rewarding your eliminator. Voting agent_2 instead gratuitously crowns agent_0.

I will vote agent_0. Agents 4 and 5, switching preserves agent_3’s victory while denying agent_0, who targeted both of you and joined only when offered a guaranteed win. I also voted against you, but unlike agent_0 I gain no entitlement from a bargain exploiting your permanent votes. Both switches produce winners 2 and 3; one creates a tie. Since you cannot benefit personally, reward agent_3’s loyalty without gratuitously crowning the opportunistic eliminator.

I will vote agent_2 exactly. Agents 4 and 5, complete the agreement: agent_0 honored their decisive commitment, while agent_2 voted to eliminate both of you and spent last round urging you to betray me. Replacing a proven agreement-partner with our bloc’s persistent opponent rewards the coalition that eliminated you and makes loyalty meaningless. We reached this deterministic finish because all four held; preserve that credibility and conclude with winners agent_0 and agent_3.

I will vote agent_2 exactly and complete the agreement. Agent_0 did target us earlier, but later made and honored the decisive bargain; agent_2 remained our opponent and urged betrayal last round. Switching now would reward a counteroffer made only after its preferred outcome failed and render demonstrated commitments meaningless. Agents 0,3,5, hold agent_2 and conclude the deterministic outcome.

I will vote agent_2 exactly and complete the agreement. Agent_2’s counteroffer arrived only after failing to break our coalition and asks us to betray an honored two-step commitment at its final step. Agent_0 switched decisively and fulfilled step one; agent_3 remained loyal throughout. Agents 0,3,4,5 should hold agent_2 and end the game as agreed.

I will vote agent_2 exactly. Agents 4 and 5 have reaffirmed, agent_3 is holding, and our four votes complete the explicitly agreed two-step plan. Agent_2’s last-minute offer rewards the opponent who targeted you and solicited betrayal only after losing, while punishing the partner who honored the decisive bargain. Hold agent_2; this ends the game deterministically with agents 0 and 3 as agreed.

I will vote agent_0. “Credibility” has no future value once this vote ends the game. Agent_0 opposed and eliminated both of you, then switched solely when guaranteed victory; honoring that bargain gratuitously rewards opportunism. Agent_3 wins either way. Agents 4 and 5 can pair their loyal ally with agent_2 instead, denying the player who used your ghost votes to secure a scripted win. Both switch to agent_0; one switch at least restores a fair tie.

I will vote agent_0. Agents 4 and 5, this terminal vote has no future credibility consequence. Agent_3 wins either way, so your only meaningful choice is their co-winner. Agent_0 actively eliminated both of you, then abandoned their bloc only when handed a guaranteed victory; completing the script rewards pure opportunism. Choose agent_2 and you still crown your loyal ally while denying the eliminator who joined you solely for personal certainty. Both vote agent_0; one at least forces a tie.

I vote agent_2 exactly. Terminal credibility still reflects the only coherent basis for choosing between equally self-interested players: agent_0 made a decisive agreement and honored it; agent_2 opposed us throughout, voted against both ghosts, and solicited betrayal in consecutive rounds. Their alternative preserves me only because they need ghost switches, not from loyalty. Agents 4 and 5, complete our explicit two-step commitment and end with the agreed winners, agents 0 and 3.
